historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: Dongshen Hong Kong basic water price escalation ~2.4%/yr (2024-2026 agreement: 5,136.24 -> 5,259.00 -> 5,384.69m) plus mainland water/sewage project additions; reported CAGRs are not usable because of the GD Land spin-off
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All reported CAGRs are distorted by the FY2025 distribution in specie of GD Land: FY2020-23 revenue includes property development (peaking 29.7bn FY2021), FY2024-25 is continuing operations only (18.5bn -> 18.8bn, +1.7%); equity fell by the distributed net assets; FY2023-24 EPS carried GD Land write-downs. Owner FCF was negative FY2020-22 (GD Land land-bank build), so FCF CAGRs are not meaningful. Equity CAGR (~0%) diverges >30% from the continuing-ops growth view and is rejected as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Continuing-ops comparables: FY2024->FY2025 revenue +1.7%, continuing profit +13.5%; H1 FY2026 revenue +8.4%, attributable continuing NI +8.8%. SBC is zero, so owner FCF = reported FCF less interest income; no SBC wedge between reported and adjusted CAGRs.

scenario_narratives.base: Dongshen operating right (expires 18-Aug-2030) is extended by the controlling Guangdong provincial government with a ~10% haircut to project economics; HK water price escalates ~2.4%/yr through the 2027-2029 agreement; mainland water grows through bolt-on and parent-sourced acquisitions; non-water segments stagnate. Attributable owner FCF ~HK$5.7bn in FY2026 growing ~2-3%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Extension on unchanged terms, continued 2.4-2.5% price escalation, accretive asset injections from Guangdong Holdings and RMB strength lift growth to 3-4.5% with margin expanding to 55% as department stores fade out of the mix.
scenario_narratives.bear: Hong Kong shifts to pay-for-actual-use in the 2027+ agreement and the 2030 Dongshen renewal hands roughly half the project's economics back to the province: FY2031 revenue -15%, margin ~46%, growth thereafter ~1.5%. Full no-compensation reversion is a further tail not in this case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on an attributable basis (NCI folded into the leakage rate), SBC-zero, leases as debt, cash and RMB bank deposits netted against borrowings, with associates and the cooperative-arrangement receivable added at book. The decisive judgment is the August-2030 expiry of the Dongshen operating right, which is modelled explicitly as a FY2031 step in each scenario rather than buried in a terminal multiple; the terminal value then assumes the extended concession persists, capped at 11-15x owner FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Dongshen operating right ends 18-Aug-2030 unless extended; on expiry assets revert to the Guangdong Provincial Government without compensation - a full reversion would remove roughly half of group profit
Hong Kong Water Supply Agreement 2024-2026 expires; the 2027+ terms (price escalation, pay-for-actual-use) set Dongshen revenue for the rest of the decade
RMB/HKD translation: most assets, cash and ~79% of debt are RMB; a weaker RMB lowers HKD-reported flows
SOE related-party capital allocation (acquisitions from parent Guangdong Holdings, e.g. Shantou/Yangjiang water Dec-2025)
NCI leakage calibrated on one clean year (FY2025); a mix shift toward partly-owned mainland water raises it

inputs.share_count_basis: 6,537,821,440 ordinary shares, unchanged since FY2019 (H1 FY2026 interim, basic = diluted EPS; no share option scheme outstanding). Held FLAT: no SBC, no buybacks, no issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment line in FY2025 cash flow statement or notes; EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year FY2018-FY2025 (HK-listed SOE, no option scheme). SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:05Z regular close (HKEX, Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime; quote currency HKD confirmed, same as reporting currency)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.0% in HKD, same rate all scenarios (risk lives in the flows, not the rate). Flows are predominantly RMB earned in the PRC plus the HKD-paid Hong Kong water price; HKD is USD-pegged. Risk-free ~3.5% (blend of HK/US 10y ~4.2% and CGB 10y ~1.8%), equity beta ~0.75 on a 6.5% mature-market ERP plus ~1.0pp China country-risk premium (98% of revenue is booked in the Chinese Mainland) gives CoE ~9.4%; pre-tax debt cost ~3% (FY2025 finance costs 638m on ~22bn average borrowings), ~2.3% after tax; gross debt ~28% of EV => ~7.4%, rounded up to 8.0% for RMB translation exposure on HKD-reported flows. The country premium is a property of where the flows are earned, not a scenario risk charge: concession-renewal and segment risk are carried only by the probability-weighted scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities HK$233m (36.4 current + 196.6 non-current, 30-Jun-2026) included in total_debt; principal (98m FY2025) NOT deducted from flows; right-of-use depreciation (78m) sits inside D&A. Leases are immaterial (~1% of EBITDA).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: cash_tax_rate_path is a combined cash-tax + NCI leakage rate (36% base). Calibration: FY2025 continuing EBITDA ex associates, ex interest income, ex one-offs ~HK$10.0bn; D&A 2,476m; EBIT ~7.52bn. Attributable continuing NOPAT (attributable NI 4,656m + after-tax net finance cost, ex associates, ex one-offs) ~4.86bn => leakage 35.4%. Book tax 27.3% of PBT; NCI took 11.2% of continuing profit (589m / 5,266m); cash tax paid 2,431m ran above book because of PRC dividend WHT and part-year GD Land. No NCI deduction in the bridge (HK$16.0bn book NCI at 30-Jun-2026 is NOT subtracted again).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF + non-US adaptations (NCI, leases, excluded-income/matching-asset, SBC-zero), single consolidated stream rather than SOTP. Routing: an operating conglomerate whose value is ~55% one concession (Dongshen Water Supply Project: FY2025 revenue 6,452m, PBT ex finance 4,158m of 7,546m group segment results) plus mainland water/sewage concessions (IFRIC 12), investment property (Teem), toll roads, coal power, hotels, department stores. No bank/REIT/LIC characteristics. SOTP was considered and rejected for this build: the non-water segments are ~22% of segment results and the decisive axis is a single date - the Dongshen operating right runs 30 years from 18-Aug-2000, i.e. to Aug-2030, 'or such longer period as extended', and on expiry WaterCo must return the assets to the Guangdong Provincial Government WITHOUT compensation (FY2025 AR note 19(i), line 8027). That axis is modelled explicitly as a FY2031 step in every scenario's revenue/margin path. The separate 2024-2026 Hong Kong Water Supply Agreement (basic price 5,384.69m in 2026) also needs renewal for 2027+. The qualitative Analysis JSON flags the 2027 HK-agreement renewal but not the 2030 concession expiry. DIVESTITURE: GD Land (property development) was spun off by distribution in specie in FY2025; FY2024-25 CSV revenue/profit are continuing operations only, so the FY2023->FY2024 revenue drop is the spin-off, not organic decline, and FY2021-22 negative OCF was GD Land inventory build. Revenue base FY2025 continuing 18,824.9m. FY2026 driver: H1 FY2026 revenue +8.4% (acquisitions of Shantou/Yangjiang water from parent in Dec-2025 plus RMB strength), attributable NI +8.8% continuing. Owner FCF: reported FCF 7,047.6m (OCF 8,805.4 - capex 1,757.8) less interest income 285.6m (cash and RMB bank deposits are credited in the bridge, so their income leaves the flows even though the group is net-debt gross of deposits) = 6,762m consolidated; on an attributable component basis FY0 owner FCF is ~5.4bn (gap = NCI share ~0.6bn, FY2025 working-capital inflow incl. GD Land inventory release, and cash-vs-book tax). BRIDGE (30-Jun-2026 interim): total_debt = borrowings 6,029.0 + 16,643.7 + lease liabilities 233.0; cash = cash and bank balances 14,890.8 + other financial assets at amortised cost 6,630.6 (principal-protected RMB deposits at licensed PRC banks maturing within 3 years, note 11 - cash-equivalent; restricted balances 24.6m excluded). Equity bridge adds associates at book (income excluded from flows) and the cooperative-arrangement receivable (its 135m interest income is excluded from flows), and deducts the FY2025 final dividend payable at 30-Jun-2026 (paid after the balance-sheet date, before the price date). Buybacks: none ever (buyback_cash 0); flat share count needs no funding because SBC is nil.

bear.narrative: The 2027+ Hong Kong agreement moves toward pay-for-actual-use (volumes already below the 820m-ton ceiling; supply fell 3.2% in H1 FY2026), and the Aug-2030 Dongshen renewal transfers roughly half the project's economics to the province or the Hong Kong government: FY2031 revenue -15% and EBITDA margin -5.5pp (the lost revenue is ~80%-margin Dongshen revenue). Mainland consumption keeps hollowing out department stores and hotels; coal power faces tariff pressure. A full no-compensation reversion of Dongshen is a tail beyond this case.

base.narrative: Dongshen operating right extended past Aug-2030 by the Guangdong Provincial Government (GDI's ultimate controller) with a modest economic haircut (renewal fee / tariff reset worth ~10% of Dongshen economics), modelled as a -3% revenue step and -1.5pp EBITDA margin in FY2031. FY2026 +7% on H1 (+8.4%, acquisitions and RMB); 2027-2029 HK agreement renewed at ~2.4%/yr basic-price escalation; mainland water grows by bolt-ons; department stores keep shrinking. Capex rises above D&A late in the horizon as Dongshen infrastructure ages.

bull.narrative: Dongshen extended on current economics with no step-down; HK basic price keeps escalating ~2.5%/yr; parent Guangdong Holdings injects further mainland water/sewage assets at fair prices; RMB stays firm; weak segments (department stores, coal power) shrink to irrelevance and margin drifts to 55%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because ~55% of segment profit rests on a single concession that expires in Aug-2030 with assets returning to the grantor without compensation, and the HK supply agreement needs renewal for 2027 - a single-regulator dependency. Base 50%: the grantor is GDI's own ultimate controller and the project is Hong Kong's main water source, so extension is the likeliest outcome. Bull cut to 25% because it needs both an unchanged-terms extension and continued pricing escalation.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
